title: Tom Brown's band and the Brown brothers' farmer costumes
summary: The Brown brothers came to Chicago, Shields swapped jobs, and band members' trades.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah. I started to ask you, did you know Tom Brown, got to hear him when you were young?
Yeah, they were terrific. They came up here. That's when Shields and Yellow Nunes switched jobs.
Yeah.
Yellow Nunes came up with the original band, and they played on the Red Lantern. A guy by the name of Harry James brought them up here, not the trumpet players. Yes, yeah.
He's still living, I think, in the audience. Yeah.
And then the Brown brothers came up with the farmer's uniforms and the straw hats, and they played. So Yellow Nunes went with the Brown brothers, and Shields went with the Dixieland.
Were they dressed like farmers? No, I didn't know that. I don't think Tom ever told me that.
And his duster's overalls are on, the straw hats.
I have seen a picture like that.
Sun hats.
Supposed to look like farmers.
Yeah.
I didn't know. I don't think Tom ever told me that. Now he's gone.
We talked about it. He's, that's what they said. This guy Murray said he was colored. He wasn't colored.
No, of course not.
That's Steve's brother. And there was another, there was Steve, Tom, there was another one. I don't think he played anything. He was a tin smith. They were all tin smiths.
Oh yeah. They even made violins and basses out of tin. Steve told me about it.
And there's another lawyer counter that used to drive a beer wagon. And he was a tuba player. Bud Lycan.
Oh yeah, Bud.
I think he's...
He died. No, I think he's in a mental hospital now. One of them is.
Then there was Jack Lycan who played left hand trombone.
I didn't know. It was Joe who still plays bass and Arnold is still around. They're the only ones I've met.
That's my, isn't that a foreign magazine?
